# Attrition ledger

**Purpose.** Account for every market-survey weighing and every PSPS household row, at
every stage of both deliverables. If a row is not in an output, this file says which step
removed it and why.

**Do not edit the numbers here.** They are generated by
`dofiles/90_diagnostics/attrition_ledger.do`, which counts rows in the files the pipeline
wrote. The machine-readable version is
`outputs/master_rename_build/summary/attrition_ledger.csv` (48 rows), and it is the source
for this document rather than the other way round. Regenerate both after any build:

```
"C:\Program Files\StataNow19\StataSE-64.exe" -e do 90_diagnostics\attrition_ledger.do
```

A hand-maintained version of this ledger went stale in three places without anything
noticing, which is why it is now derived.

## How to read it

Three record types, and keeping them apart is the point of the file.

| `record_type` | means |
|---|---|
| `stage` | a real drop: rows in, rows dropped, rows out, and a reason |
| `aggregation` | the **unit of observation changes**. `rows_dropped` is deliberately empty |
| `detail` | a named figure or case worth following, with its current status |

**Aggregation is not attrition.** 11,290 weighings becoming 2,559 reference-set rows is
not a 77% loss; it is a change of grain from a weighing to a (case × size) group, and each
group publishes one row holding its median. The weighings sum back exactly — `n_g` over
the published rows totals 11,290. Subtracting across an aggregation row produces a
loss that never happened.

**Every row states its `grain`.** Counts at different grains must not be differenced. A
count of *cases* and a count of *weighings* disagree legitimately, and one case below
(CAPIZ / TAPAZ chicken) exists specifically because a case can survive at one grain and
vanish at another. The project's pooling grain is

> province × municipality × item × `harmonized_nsu_unit` × `corrected_unit`

## The shared market-survey chain

Both outcomes read the same weighings up to this point.

```
   11,495   raw weighings
      -62   stage 1   03_clean_ms.do
   11,433   arrival
      -98   stage 2   07_cpi_factor.do          <- both outcomes read this file
   11,335   priced weighings
```

| stage | step | drops | reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1a | 4 | comment-flagged data-entry errors and other hand-identified drops |
| 1 | 1b | 58 | labels that are not non-standard units — standard quantity 31, ambiguous quantity 22, not a unit 5 |
| 2 | 2 | 98 | price-quantity weighings whose recorded price was not the amount handed over |

**Stage 1b is dropped before the magnitude snap**, so a non-unit label never pollutes an
anchor pool. The rule belongs to `02_drop_non_nsu_labels.py`; the rows and their reasons
are listed in `excluded_standard_unit_obs.xlsx`.

**Stage 2 is the only place those 98 rows are dropped, and both outcomes depend on it.**
Skipping `07_cpi_factor.do` does not merely cost `cpi_factor`; it silently readmits
weighings whose recorded price was not the price the enumerator handed over. 23
vendor-priced rows are **rescued** rather than dropped, where they were their case's only
rung — losing a case entirely is worse than the problem the drop solves — and
`price_source` records which is which.

**"No crosswalk row" is a defect category, not an attrition category.** The crosswalk merge
has 0 unmatched rows and `03_clean_ms.do` hard-stops if that ever changes, so every stage-1
drop leaves against a stated reason rather than by falling out of a join.

## Outcome 1

```
   11,335   priced weighings
      -45   stage 3   Outcome 1's own exclusions
   11,290   entering the collapse
 ->  2,559  published reference-set rows        (AGGREGATION, not attrition)
```

| step | drops | reason |
|---|---|---|
| 3a | 8 | `corrected_weight` is `.c` — no interpretation rescues the reading. Set by hand in `05_manual_corrections.do` rather than deleted, so they remain accountable |
| 3b | 33 | `unique_mun_price` weighings. A unique municipal price is not a size, and Outcome 1 publishes grams **by size**. **Outcome 2 keeps these rows** — they are price-quantity weighings with a real `pull_price` |
| 3c | 4 | the price-quantity rows of the one mixed-branch cell, ILOILO / TIGBAUAN carrot. Outcome 1 takes that cell's size-based rows and Outcome 2 its price-quantity ones, so neither outcome mixes branches inside a case |

Two published figures that are **not** attrition: **518** rows rest on fewer than `THIN`
weighings (`d_thin`), and **488** cells lost their size ladder to the L1 collapse
(`fallback_level = 1`). Both ship, flagged, with `n_g` alongside.

**Total real drops across the market-survey chain: 205.**

## Outcome 2 — the supply side

Outcome 2 forks from **stage 2**, not stage 3: it keeps the `unique_mun_price` weighings
and slices on `branch` rather than on the field's size labels.

| branch | weighings | groups | grain |
|---|---|---|---|
| size-based | 10,141 | 2,633 | case × group |
| price-quantity | 1,114 | 368 → **1,093** after crossing with interview months | case × price point × month |
| conventional | 80 | 24 | case |
| | | **3,750** lookup rows | |

`branch` is not `weighing_approach`: 99 field-conventional cases whose (item, unit) pair
mixes approaches elsewhere are processed as size-based (issue #28, A12). That is why Branch
C is 80 weighings and 24 cases rather than 468 and 123.

**495 of Branch S's 2,633 rows are price points that carry no weight** — an emptied part of
the cut, or a refused unique price (A16). They are in the table on purpose: a household
matches the *nearest* point, so removing them would push it onto the next point along and
convert it at a weight belonging to a different rung.

Issue #11's no-inflation variant is a second lookup of 3,025 rows. It drops the month
dimension rather than setting the factor to 1, because without a restatement nothing
month-specific is left on any branch.

## Outcome 2 — the demand side

```
  245,051   PSPS consumption rows
  129,094   food rows                     (item_type == 1)
   87,959   household x item x slot rows with a usable quantity
```

Prepped food is recorded in `fd_cons_5a` as a **number of times consumed**, with no unit
and no quantity, so it cannot be converted from an NSU at all and is not in the food count.

The consumption module records three parallel acquisition slots — 2 purchased, 3 own
production, 4 gift — so one food row can yield up to three rows. Only slots with a
non-missing, non-zero quantity are kept, which is the filter `NSU_Analysis.R` used when it
built the price file and therefore the denominator every figure on issue #30 rests on.

Every row then takes exactly one of five conversion paths, **asserted exhaustive and
mutually exclusive**:

| path | rows | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| standard unit — converted from the unit's own name | 52,489 | all converted (#14) |
| **non-standard unit — needs the market survey** | **35,448** | **34,916 converted, 532 refused** |
| not an NSU at all | 22 | unconvertible by definition |
| no unit given by the respondent | 0 | — |
| NSU label with no crosswalk row in this cell | 0 | — |

The last row being empty is worth stating: **every unit label a PSPS household reported
with a usable quantity resolves.** It follows from the crosswalk being built from the price
file, which is itself built from these same PSPS responses — but it had never been checked
at the cell grain, and the path exists so a future vintage's unfamiliar label appears as a
number rather than as rows that quietly convert to nothing.

### Where the 35,448 went

| route | rows |
|---|---|
| matched price point | 28,961 |
| fallback: province pool | 5,410 |
| fallback: national pool | 361 |
| fallback: cell pooled (an emptied part of the cut) | 184 |
| refused: A11 spelling gap | 304 |
| refused: unique price (A16) | 117 |
| refused: nothing anywhere | 111 |

By rung: **L0** 28,961 · **L1** 110 · **L2** 5,484 · **L3** 361. From L1 down the
household's own price is not used at all — every household in the cell receives the same
grams whatever it paid (A15).

**1,283 rows had their price ratio clamped** (A18). Clamped and kept, never dropped:
`d_cap` marks them and `r_h_raw` keeps the uncapped ratio.

A refused row is **reported, never imputed and never silently redirected** to another
price point. The list is `psps_unconvertible.csv`.

## The price-file side

Issue #8 asks for the price data accounted for as well as the market survey.

| | |
|---|---|
| price rows as delivered | 5,412 |
| price points after the union on value and the ₱20 single-linkage merge | 3,171 |
| …of those, refused (a unique price with no weighing behind it) | 238 |
| priced-but-unweighed spellings | 305 |
| …diverging from their case's weighed price level by ≥ 2× (A11) | 60 |

Rows on a label the non-NSU trim removed are dropped. Rows on a spelling never *weighed*
in the cell are excluded from group construction — they carry no weight, so they cannot
inform a weight moment — but retained for the A11 gap flag.

One price row carries R's literal string `NA`. It is a placeholder, not a lost price:
NEGROS OCCIDENTAL / MANAPLA / Loaf Bread / Large, every numeric field `NA`, and its case
keeps its real ₱120 unique price and ₱90 province median.

## Named cases

Four cases are followed individually because they are the ones where a naive count
misleads. Each is **re-checked against the current build** on every run rather than
restated, and two have since resolved.

**NEGROS OCCIDENTAL / ENRIQUE B. MAGALONA / ice cream / `putos` / mL — RESOLVED.** This
cell used to be lost in stage 2 to a rescue-rule grain mismatch: the rule decided "does
this case keep a preloaded rung" *without* `corrected_unit`, so the gram side's preloaded
row shielded the millilitre side, whose only price-quantity row was then dropped.
`corrected_unit` is now in the rescue key and the cell survives.

**CAPIZ / TAPAZ / chicken / `whole (chicken)` — still live.** 4 of its 9 rows have a blank
field weight and therefore no `corrected_unit`, which puts them in their own
(case × `corrected_unit` = missing) group. The case is lost at the fine grain while its
gram split survives, so a count of *cases* differs between the two grains here. This is
the concrete reason every row of the ledger states its grain.

**Harmonized unit `putos (mix vegetable)` — its own case, not part of the carrot
narrative.** It is a fold target collecting rows from **more than one item** — cabbage and
carrot — across 15 cells and 53 weighings. The ILOILO / DUEÑAS cabbage cell that had no
price-file row was a different problem, resolved by dropping an ambiguous label at source
(issue #22).

**The crosswalk merge itself — 0 unmatched**, and `03_clean_ms.do` halts if that changes.

## What this ledger does not do

It counts rows, and a row count is not the whole of what a reader needs.

**The uncertainty attached to a weight is carried separately, and it is carried.** Roughly
one weighing in seven is disputed, anchor-flagged or unusable. `08_branch.do` defines the
four flags from build columns, and both deliverables publish them per row — the reference
set and the Outcome 2 lookup as `n_disputed` / `n_flagged` / `n_uncertain` /
`share_uncertain`, and every converted household row as `nu_used` at the fallback rung that
supplied its weight. See A20 and issue #35. This ledger does not aggregate those counts,
because a stage total would mix weighings that were questioned with weighings that were
dropped, and the two are different facts about different rows.

**It does not say whether a published weight differs from what the enumerator typed.**
That is `magnitude_corrected` in `weight_correction_report.csv`, and it is deliberately not
one of the uncertainty flags: most corrections are decimal slips the pipeline exists to
repair, so a correction count read as a defect rate would misdescribe the work. No
deliverable currently carries it.
